$$p(x)=-1,\quad q(x)=e^{\left(x+1\right)},\quad n=2.$$

Divide by $y^{2}$ and set $z=y^{-1}$. The chain rule gives

$$I(x)=e^{\int 1\,\mathrm{d}x}=e^{\left(x+1\right)}.$$

Thus

$$z=C \cdot e^{- \left(x+1\right)} - \frac{e^{\left(x+1\right)}}{2}.$$

Finally, substitute $z=y^{-1}$ and solve for $y$:

$$y=\frac{2 \cdot e^{\left(x+1\right)}}{2 \cdot C - e^{2 \cdot \left(x+1\right)}}.$$
